subject: Entitlement carveouts & crediting for sovereign residency/HSM
messages:
From: Claire Park <procurement@sovereignhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify how you want to treat implementation fee vs recurring residency surcharge

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — Sovereign execs liked the latency profiles and the HSM story. Before we loop legal and procurement approvals, we need a clear pricing construct for the residency + HSM work. Specifically: 

- How will you treat the one-time implementation/onboarding fee? Can that be credited against committed usage? If so, over what period?
- If we require data residency in our EU and US sovereign regions initially, do you charge a per-region residency surcharge or a one-time migration fee?
- HSM: seat licensing vs per-request billing — what's the recommended approach for a two-year agreement?

We are preparing an internal TCO comparison and need a concrete example we can present (numbers are fine to be placeholders). Also send any standard SOW / cost breakdown you use.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement has a tight window.

Best,
Claire
Procurement, Sovereign Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <procurement@sovereignhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Clarify how you want to treat implementation fee vs recurring residency surcharge

Hi Claire — thanks for the note and the thoughtful questions. High level answers + a suggested commercial path below; attaching a short SOW and a simple spreadsheet that models three options.

Attachments: SOW_SovereignResidency_v1.pdf (SOW stub, implementation milestones), residency_cost_breakdown_Q1.xlsx (cost model)

Summary options (numbers illustrative):
1) Upfront implementation fee, fully amortized: $120k one-time onboarding (install + validation + HSM integration). We can offer a credit of 60% of that fee applied against committed hosted spend across the first 12 months (applies only to hosted invoices, not HSM seat invoices).

2) Reduced upfront + monthly residency surcharge: $60k upfront + $6k/month residency surcharge per region (covers dedicated infra + network egress controls). The upfront is 40% creditable against committed hosted spend over first 6 months.

3) No upfront, higher recurring: waive upfront if you sign a 24-month committed consumption contract (e.g., $X committed monthly) and take a $10k/month residency surcharge; we then treat the waived onboarding as a sales credit amortized over first 12 months of committed spend.

HSM licensing: we recommend seat-based HSM for initial rollouts where you need FIPS/HSM-backed key management (one-time provisioning + monthly seat fee). For high-volume signing, we can offer a hybrid model: lower seat fee + per-request egress surcharge. Ben (cc'd) has the seat slab pricing.

Key commercial levers we usually offer:
- Credit % of implementation fee (40-75%) to be applied only to committed hosted usage in Year 1.
- Residency surcharge can be set as monthly per-region or amortized as a one-time migration fee — your preference.
- Entitlement carveouts: if you bring existing on-prem workloads that won't use Redwood-hosted model runtime, we can carve those out and not charge residency for them, but there are measurement clauses.

If you prefer, we can propose a blended option that reduces near-term cash outlay and applies credits against committed usage. If that sounds close, I can put a proposal in HubSpot and send for signature.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Claire Park <procurement@sovereignhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Clarify how you want to treat implementation fee vs recurring residency surcharge

Claire / Karthik — quick note on HSM and entitlement carveouts: 

- HSM seats: standard slab pricing is $2,500/seat/month for provisioned FIPS-backed HSMs (includes key rotation tooling and audits). For a 24-month commit we can offer 15% off seat list for the first 12 months. Alternatively, if customer has existing HSM/Thales we can integrate and only bill the gateway + per-request usage (~$0.0015/request).

- Entitlement carveouts: we can exclude pre-existing on-prem inference (if you certify it in the inventory) from residency surcharges. That typically requires an inventory CSV (we can provide a template) and a quarterly reconciliation clause. For carveouts we also require a small audit execution fee ($3k/quarter) to validate usage.

- Credit mechanics: operationally, credits are issued via invoice credit memos applied to hosted usage invoices. Example: $72k credit (60% of $120k) applied across first 12 invoices until exhausted. If the customer terminates early, unused credits are forfeited.

I'm happy to bake specific numbers into the model you requested.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Operations
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Claire Park <procurement@sovereignhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Clarify how you want to treat implementation fee vs recurring residency surcharge

Karthik / Ben — thanks — the options help. Two legal items before we proceed to procurement approval: 

1) Retention SLA for audit logs: we need a contractual commitment for 7 years retention with exportability and chain-of-custody metadata. Is that something Redwood will commit to for an enterprise add-on?

2) Credit enforcement: procurement prefers credits that survive termination (i.e., convertible to cash-back pro rata) for a limited carveout window. We understand forfeiture is standard, but can we meet halfway: unused credits convert to a 50% cash-back return if Redwood terminates for convenience within the first 12 months?

If you can send a redlineable term sheet (or indicate that you'll accept these two points), we'll circulate with Finance and Legal.

Also, please confirm the SOW milestones and acceptance criteria (we want explicit validation tests for HSM integration).

Regards,
Claire Park
Sovereign Health — Procurement
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <procurement@sovereignhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Clarify how you want to treat implementation fee vs recurring residency surcharge

Claire — appreciate the clear asks. Proposed compromise below (we're aiming for redlineable language I can drop into the term sheet):

Agreed commercial path (final proposal):
- Implementation/onboarding fee: $95,000 one-time. 60% creditable ($57,000) applied against hosted committed usage invoices over the first 12 months.
- Residency charge: $4,500/month/region (US/US-sovereign/EU-sovereign) — applies only to Redwood-hosted model runtime. Pre-existing on-prem inference (inventory to be provided by Sovereign) is excluded subject to quarterly reconciliation and a $3,000/quarter audit validation fee.
- HSM: seat model by default (provisioned), $2,125/seat/month with 12-month 10% discount on a 24-month commitment. Optionally integrate existing HSMs and bill gateway + per-request at $0.0013/request.
- Audit log retention: Redwood will commit to 7-year retention for enterprise add-on customers; logs will be exportable with chain-of-custody metadata. We'll include a data export SLA in the term sheet and acceptance criteria in the SOW.
- Credit survivability on termination: If Redwood terminates for convenience within the first 12 months, unused credits convert to a 50% cash-back payable within 90 days (this is our compromise). If customer terminates early, credits remain forfeited.

SOW milestones (high level):
1) Kickoff + inventory review (week 1–2)
2) HSM provisioning & integration (week 3–6) — acceptance tests: key provisioning, signing validation, audit log generation
3) Residency validation & traffic routing test (week 7–9)
4) Final acceptance & production cutover (week 10)

Next steps: I will upload this as a proposed term sheet in HubSpot (link below) and prep a DocuSign packet with the SOW. If that aligns with you, Claire, I'll get Legal to include the redlineable term sheet and Ben will prepare an invoice schedule.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/DEAL-8291
DocuSign (draft): https://docusign.com/packet/RED-8291-SOV

Thanks — I can get the draft ready by Monday.

Regards,
